subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Pluto's Demotion
description: Learn Pluto's Demotion in one minute.

hook.text: In 2006, Pluto was stripped of its planet title and reclassified as a dwarf planet. Millions were furious.

buildup.text: Astronomers found dozens of Pluto-sized objects beyond Neptune. If Pluto counted, so would they all.

discovery.text: The IAU set three rules for planethood. Pluto failed the third: clearing other objects from its orbit.

twist.text: New Horizons flew past Pluto in 2015, revealing ice mountains, glaciers, and a heart-shaped plain.

climax.text: The debate continues. Some scientists say Pluto's geology makes it more interesting than most planets.

punchline.text: Demoted by committee. Redeemed by a spacecraft.

quiz.question: Why was Pluto reclassified as a dwarf planet?
options: It hasn't cleared other objects from its orbital neighborhood
It was found to be smaller than originally measured
It doesn't orbit the Sun in the same plane as other planets

details.summary: In 2006, the International Astronomical Union reclassified Pluto from the ninth planet to a 'dwarf planet' because it hasn't cleared its orbital neighborhood of other debris.
details.whyItMatters: Pluto's reclassification forced a rigorous definition of 'planet' for the first time and highlighted the Kuiper Belt's richness. The debate continues and reveals how scientific classification evolves as knowledge grows.
takeaways: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006 by the IAU
It didn't meet the criterion of clearing its orbital neighborhood
The discovery of Eris and other Kuiper Belt objects prompted the change

faq.question: What are the three criteria for a planet?
faq.answer: The IAU's 2006 definition requires a planet to: (1) orbit the Sun, (2) have enough mass for a nearly round shape (hydrostatic equilibrium), and (3) have cleared the neighborhood around its orbit of other debris. Pluto meets the first two but shares the Kuiper Belt with thousands of similar objects.

faq.question: Do most astronomers agree with Pluto's demotion?
faq.answer: Opinion remains divided. Some argue the definition is flawed — using 'clearing the neighborhood' disadvantages distant objects where clearing takes longer. Others note that without the distinction, the solar system would have dozens of planets.
